title: An easy Miraflores day built around lunch at Huaca Pucllana
dayIntro: This day stays inside Miraflores and asks little of your legs. It starts with sourdough and coffee, then takes in the Pacific from the top of the cliffs at Parque del Amor. Its weight falls on a long lunch of Peruvian classics at a restaurant set inside Huaca Pucllana, an archaeological site of the Lima culture. The afternoon trades views for the craft galleries on Avenida Petit Thouars, then leaves a long gap to rest. Dinner is deliberately small. Every move between stops is a short taxi ride, and nothing on the route involves cliff stairs or a walk down to the beach.
tripRole: First full day: a low-effort introduction to Miraflores with a Peruvian lunch as the main event. Historic-centre culture is kept for Day 2 and Barranco, art and a later evening for Day 3.
scheduleLabel: Illustrative evergreen plan; check opening days before use

stops.name: El Pan de la Chola (Alcanfores)
stops.whyHere: A gentle opener in central Miraflores, open from early morning every day, with a short taxi ride to the clifftop park.
stops.readerCopy: El Pan de la Chola is a Lima bakery that works with natural fermentation and local flours, some of them ground on its own stone mill. Its Alcanfores branch opens at 7am every day. Keep breakfast simple: a croissant or a morning bun with a cappuccino, or avocado and egg on sourdough toast if you want more. The point is to eat lightly. Lunch is the meal this day is built around, and anything heavier now works against it.
whatToDo: Order coffee with a pastry such as a classic croissant or a morning bun
Choose a toast, such as avocado and egg or hummus, if a pastry is not enough
practicalNotes: As listed on the branch menu in September 2026: classic croissant PEN 8, cappuccino PEN 11, avocado and egg toast PEN 24.
The bakery states that allergens are present in its kitchens and keeps an allergen sheet at the counter.
stops.selectionReason: It is an official Miraflores branch of a sourdough bakery with posted daily hours starting at 7am. Its branch menu lists coffee, pastries and light toasts, which meets the 'light breakfast or coffee' and 'bakery' criteria. It was chosen over the chain's La Mar branches because Alcanfores is on the southern, clifftop side of central Miraflores, which suits the morning route.

stops.name: Parque del Amor (Love Park)
stops.whyHere: The low-effort coastal highlight: an ocean view from the top of the cliffs, reached by taxi, with no beach descent.
stops.readerCopy: Parque del Amor sits on Malecón Cisneros at the edge of the Miraflores cliffs, so the Pacific is laid out below you without a single step down to the shore. The park opened on 14 February 1993 around El Beso, Víctor Delfín's large sculpture of a couple kissing. Its tiled surrounds carry lines by Peruvian poets including Martín Adán and César Moro, and the design draws on Gaudí's Park Güell. An hour is enough: look at the sea, read the walls, then cross to Marcelo Wong's Cupido sculpture opposite.
whatToDo: Take in the Pacific view from the clifftop
Look at El Beso and read the poets' lines set into the tiled surrounds
Cross to see Marcelo Wong's Cupido sculpture directly opposite the park
practicalNotes: Entry is free and the park is open 24 hours; the recommended visiting time is 8am–9pm.
Public toilets and food and drink kiosks are listed at the park.
Ramps are listed for visitors with physical disabilities.
stops.selectionReason: Official municipal and MINCETUR records place the park at the edge of the Malecón Cisneros cliffs, with a view of the Pacific, free entry and 24-hour access. This meets the 'coastal view from above' and 'no beach descent' requirements. The park also has substance beyond the view (the Delfín sculpture and the poetry mosaics). Larcomar was rejected because it is a shopping centre and would overlap with the afternoon shopping stop.

stops.name: Restaurante Huaca Pucllana
stops.addressOrMeetingPoint: Calle General Borgoño, block 8, Huaca Pucllana, Miraflores, Lima
stops.whyHere: The food anchor of the day: an à la carte Peruvian menu in a setting inside an archaeological site, all within Miraflores.
stops.readerCopy: Restaurante Huaca Pucllana is set inside Huaca Pucllana, a site of the Lima culture dating to between 200 and 700 AD, and you eat with a view of the ruins. The menu is à la carte, so you can linger over a long lunch without committing to a tasting menu. Order from the section headed Tradición peruana, which includes chupe de camarones, cau cau, lomo saltado and seco de lomo, or start with a classic ceviche. The restaurant says 7.6% of its sales go toward restoring the monument.
whatToDo: Book a table ahead through the restaurant's official booking link
Order from the Tradición peruana section, or begin with the classic ceviche
Take your time; nothing is scheduled until mid-afternoon
practicalNotes: Posted hours: Monday to Saturday 12pm–10pm, Sunday 12pm–5pm.
Bookings are taken through the link on the restaurant's website, or by email at reservas@resthuacapucllana.com.
On the menu posted in September 2026, the Tradición peruana dishes cost PEN 51–74 and the classic ceviche PEN 55. Prices include taxes and service.
stops.selectionReason: The official site identifies this as a Peruvian restaurant inside Huaca Pucllana in Miraflores. The official menu is à la carte with a dedicated Peruvian-tradition section, and El Comercio reports its view over the Lima-culture archaeological site. This meets 'distinctly Peruvian', 'a la carte' and 'special setting' without leaving Miraflores or using Barranco. Its posted hours cover a noon lunch on every day of the week.

stops.name: Boulevard Artesanal de Miraflores (Avenida Petit Thouars craft galleries)
stops.addressOrMeetingPoint: Av. Petit Thouars, blocks 52–55, Miraflores; start at Mercado Indio, Av. Petit Thouars 5245
stops.whyHere: It contrasts with the morning: streets and shops instead of a view, and it is easy to cut short before the rest break.
stops.readerCopy: After a view and a long lunch, the afternoon turns to shopping. Blocks 52 to 55 of Avenida Petit Thouars hold 14 craft galleries with more than 1,500 artisans between them. Their work comes from across Peru: woodcarving, textiles, ceramics, carved gourds (mates burilados), silverwork and retablos. This is shopping aimed at visitors rather than a neighbourhood market, and it is easy to cut short. Walk one side, cross, walk back, and leave when you have had enough. Indian Market and Inka Plaza are both on the 5300 block.
whatToDo: Browse the galleries between Mercado Indio at number 5245 and the 5400 block
Look for regional work such as mates burilados, retablos and silverwork
Stop when you have had enough; nothing later depends on this stop
practicalNotes: Mercado Indio, at number 5245, posts opening hours of every day until 8pm.
stops.selectionReason: The Miraflores municipal tourism site lists this handicraft boulevard, its location on blocks 52–55 and the range of crafts sold. It adds shops and street-level texture and does not repeat the morning's scenic park. It can be shortened at will. Mercado Indio's posted daily hours cover the afternoon slot.

stops.name: Pardos Chicken (Benavides)
stops.whyHere: A casual, lighter recovery meal in central Miraflores after the main lunch, open early enough for an 18:30 table every day.
stops.readerCopy: Dinner is small on purpose. Pardos Chicken is a Peruvian chain built around pollo a la brasa. Its branch on Avenida Benavides opens every day from noon until at least 11pm, so an early table is no problem. After the lunch at Huaca Pucllana, order from the sandwich or salad sections, or share the chicken between two. An hour is plenty. This is the meal that lets you eat well today and still have energy for tomorrow.
whatToDo: Order from the sandwich or salad sections, or share a chicken order
Keep dinner to about an hour
practicalNotes: Posted hours: Monday to Thursday 12pm–12am, Friday and Saturday 12pm–1am, Sunday 12pm–11pm.
The branch takes reservations by phone (241-0215 or 998 158 770) and by email (reservas@pardosbenavides.com).
stops.selectionReason: The official branch page confirms the Miraflores address and daily hours that cover an 18:30 dinner. The chain's official menu includes sandwich and salad sections, so the reader can keep the meal lighter than lunch while still eating distinctly Peruvian food. La Lucha Sanguchería was considered as a lighter sandwich option but rejected because its official site shows no current hours.

stops.name: Haití (café, bar and restaurant)
stops.whyHere: An optional, conversation-friendly café-bar finish near dinner in central Miraflores, open well past the day's end.
stops.readerCopy: Haití has faced the Parque Central de Miraflores since 23 February 1962. It is a café, bar and restaurant that grew out of a café opened on Plaza Pizarro in 1952. It stays open until 1am every day, so you are nowhere near closing time: take a table and order an espresso or a glass from the wine list. Skip it if the day has already been enough. Nothing later depends on it.
whatToDo: Order an espresso or a drink from the wine list
Leave by about 20:30 to reach your hotel by 21:00
stops.selectionReason: The official site describes Haití as a family-run restaurant, café and bar with a long history on the Parque Central de Miraflores, a wine list and daily hours to 1am. That suits a quiet, social finish that is not a club. It stays optional; removing it leaves the required day intact.

transfers.note: Exact hotel is unknown. The schedule leaves 09:00–09:30 for this leg; take a taxi if it is more than a short walk.

claims.text: El Pan de la Chola's Alcanfores branch is at Calle Alcanfores 410, Miraflores, and posts hours of Monday to Sunday, 7am–9pm.

The Alcanfores branch menu lists espresso-based coffees, pastries including a classic croissant and a morning bun, and toasts including avocado and egg and hummus. It states that its breads are 100% sourdough.
El Pan de la Chola says it respects natural dough fermentation and uses local flours and cereals, some of which it mills in its workshop on a traditional stone mill.
The Alcanfores branch menu, accessed 2026-09-15, lists a classic croissant at PEN 8, a cappuccino at PEN 11 and avocado and egg toast at PEN 24.
The branch menu states that all products are prepared where allergens are present and that an allergen sheet is available at the counter.

Parque del Amor is on Malecón Cisneros (block 4), Miraflores. It was inaugurated on 14 February 1993 and centres on the sculpture El Beso by Víctor Delfín. Its surrounds are decorated with verses by Peruvian poets including Martín Adán and César Moro.
The park was built at the edge of the Malecón Cisneros cliffs and offers a view of the Pacific Ocean. Its design is inspired by Gaudí's Park Güell in Barcelona.
The MINCETUR inventory lists free entry, 24-hour opening with a recommended visiting time of 8am–9pm, restrooms, food and drink kiosks, and ramps for people with physical disabilities.
The sculpture Cupido by Peruvian artist Marcelo Wong stands directly across from the park.
Restaurante Huaca Pucllana is a Peruvian-cuisine restaurant located inside Huaca Pucllana at Calle General Borgoño, block 8, Miraflores.
The official site lists hours of Monday to Saturday 12:00pm–10:00pm and Sunday 12:00pm–5:00pm. It provides a booking link and the email reservas@resthuacapucllana.com.
The official menu is à la carte. Its 'Tradición peruana' section includes chupe de camarones, cau cau Don Arturo, lomo saltado and seco de lomo, and the menu also lists a classic ceviche.
The menu states that the company contributes 7.6% of its sales to the restoration of the historic monument, and that prices include taxes and service.
On the official menu PDF accessed 2026-09-15, the 'Tradición peruana' dishes range from PEN 51 to PEN 74 and the classic ceviche is PEN 55.
The restaurant offers a view of the archaeological site where the Lima culture (200–700 AD) developed.

The Miraflores handicraft boulevard occupies blocks 52–55 of Av. Petit Thouars and houses more than 1,500 artisans in 14 galleries. Its crafts from across the country include woodcarving, textiles, ceramics, mates burilados, jewellery, silverwork and retablos.
Galleries listed by the municipality include Centro Artesanal Adaprep (Av. Petit Thouars 5245), Indian Market (Av. Petit Thouars 5321-50) and Inka Plaza (Av. Petit Thouars 5330).
Mercado Indio, at Av. Petit Thouars 5245, lists opening every day until 20:00. The same page gives the opening time as 09:00 in one place and 09:30 in another.
The Miraflores municipal tourism site presents the Av. Petit Thouars handicraft boulevard as the district's place for handmade crafts and souvenirs.

Pardos Chicken Benavides is at Av. Benavides 730. Its posted hours are Monday–Thursday 12:00pm–12:00am, Friday–Saturday 12:00pm–1:00am and Sunday 12:00pm–11:00pm. It takes reservations at 241-0215 / 998158770 and reservas@pardosbenavides.com.
Pardos Chicken presents itself as a pollo a la brasa restaurant. Its online menu categories include sánguches, ensaladas and anticuchos.
Haití is at Av. Diagonal 160, Miraflores, and posts hours of Monday to Sunday, 07:30am–01:00am.
Haití describes itself as a restaurant, café and bar. Its café began operating on Plaza Pizarro in early 1952, and on 23 February 1962 it opened opposite the Parque Central de Miraflores.
Haití offers espresso coffee, Mediterranean, Peruvian and international dishes, and a wine list.

feasibility.detail: Every selected venue posts hours that cover its scheduled slot on all seven days: the bakery (daily 7am–9pm), the park (open 24 hours), lunch (Mon–Sat from noon, Sun noon–5pm), Mercado Indio (daily to 8pm), Pardos (daily from noon) and Haití (daily 7:30am–1am). The condition is that the lunch hours are official, but secondary listings disagree. Mercado Indio's hours come from a 2023 page, and the other galleries' hours were not checked. Confirm lunch by phone or booking before relying on a Monday.

feasibility.topic: Total time including transfers and rest
feasibility.detail: Scheduled activity runs from 09:30 to 20:30. It includes 45 + 60 + 105 + 75 + 60 + 45 minutes at stops, five taxi legs estimated at 30–90 minutes in total, and one 165-minute rest window. There are 30-minute buffers at 09:00–09:30 and 20:30–21:00 for the unknown hotel legs. If the optional evening is dropped, the day ends around 19:30.

Every leg between stops is planned as a taxi, so walking is limited to moving within each stop. The coastal stop is at the top of the cliffs, with no stairs or beach descent. The condition is that walking distances between stops were not routed, so the reader should not swap taxis for walks without checking.

The day has one main meal: an à la carte Peruvian lunch. Breakfast is a light bakery stop. Dinner is at a casual chain whose menu includes sandwich and salad sections. Keeping dinner lighter than lunch depends on what the reader orders, which the copy steers but cannot guarantee.

All six stops are in Miraflores, and none are in Barranco or the historic centre. The route runs from central Miraflores to the clifftop, north to Huaca Pucllana, back to Petit Thouars, then to central Miraflores for dinner and the evening. Each leg is a short taxi ride rather than a cross-city transfer.

The exact hotel is unspecified, so the first leg (to breakfast), the final leg (from Haití or from Pardos), and any hotel visit during the rest window cannot be timed. The 30-minute buffers are assumptions and fit only a hotel within central Miraflores.

Lunch overlooks Huaca Pucllana but does not include a site visit. If Day 2's substantial cultural visit is planned at Huaca Pucllana, it would partly repeat Day 1. Craft shopping and the Parque Central area are now covered and should not recur. Day 3 in Barranco should avoid another clifftop viewpoint that repeats Parque del Amor.
No bookings were made and no live availability was checked. Lunch has an official booking channel and is the only reservation worth making in advance. Pardos also accepts reservations.
